9. Call RenderEntityDisplayScreen() to render current state
10. Call InitializeEntityCharacterAndRenderUI() to update character display
11. Return 1 (success status)

Parameters:
None - operates entirely on global state variables

Returns:
int - Always returns 1 (success status)

Global Variables:
- 0x6fa64dbc: Entity display counter (incremented per cycle)
- 0x6fa64db0: Current entity/slot index (incremented when within bounds)
- 0x6fa65ed4: Frame index counter (incremented every call)
- 0x6fa65ed0: Maximum frame count (upper bound for counter)

Special Cases:
- When displayCounter + frameIndex >= maxFrameCount: rendering is skipped entirely
- Slot index increments only when less than (maxFrameCount - 1)
- Both rendering functions are called together as a unit when condition is met

0x6FA4C310.name: UpdateEntityDisplayFrame
0x6FA4C310.comment:
Updates display frame with entity rendering and UI updates.

Algorithm:
1. Load first countdown counter (DAT_6fa65ed4)
2. If counter > 0, decrement it and store back
3. Load second countdown counter (DAT_6fa64db0)
4. If counter > 0, decrement it and store back
5. Call RenderEntityDisplayScreen() to update display
6. Call InitializeEntityCharacterAndRenderUI() to refresh UI
7. Return status code 1 (success)

Purpose: Main frame update function that decrements timing counters
and triggers display/UI refresh cycles. Used for controlling animation
frame timing and UI state updates.

Returns: int - Status code (1 = success)

Structure Layout (Global State):
Offset  Size  Field Name              Type    Description
------  ----  ----------------------  ------  --------------------------------
6fa65ed4 4    first_countdown_timer   int     Frame counter, decrements each
                                              frame until 0
6fa64db0 4    second_countdown_timer  int     Additional timing counter for
                                              UI refresh cycles
------  ----  ----------------------  ------  --------------------------------

0x6FA4C370.name: InitializeGameConfiguration
0x6FA4C370.comment:
Initializes game configuration and core game state by setting up configuration parameters and calling initialization routines.

Algorithm:
1. Call ResetGameStateAndUIControls to clean up any existing state
2. Call CopyMemoryWithAlignment to configure game data with "ProjectD2" and "Diablo_II" settings
3. Call additional game initialization routine
4. Return success status (1)

Parameters:
None - Called with no parameters using __stdcall calling convention

Returns:
int - Returns 1 (success) after successful initialization

Special Cases:
- First parameter (0x7fffffff) appears to be a configuration limit or max value
- Configuration strings "ProjectD2" and "Diablo_II" identify the game project
- "Preferred_Realm" setting configured with null value during initialization
- Function uses __stdcall convention with RET 0x4 indicating 4 bytes of stack cleanup

Notes:
This is a high-level initialization wrapper that orchestrates game startup by calling lower-level configuration and state management routines. It appears to be called during game launch to establish the initial game environment.

0x6FA4C3C0.name: CreateUnitFromDispatchedCommand
0x6FA4C3C0.comment:
Dispatches a command and creates a new unit with initialization.

Algorithm:
1. Push ECX to save callee-saved register
2. Load context constant 0x2b3b into ECX register (game context ID)
3. Call dispatch_command_handler() with context to retrieve unit name string
4. Load global unit counter from 0x6fa65ed0 into ECX
5. Prepare unit class byte (0x12) and type code (0x2) on stack
6. Get address of stack-allocated structure parameter (offset +0x8)
7. Push unit name result (EAX) and structure address as parameters
8. Store class/type value at [ESP + 0x10]
9. Store global unit counter value at global 0x6fa64db8
10. Call CreateAndInitializeUnit() with parameters: unit name, class/type structure pointer, type code 0x2, class code 0x12
11. Pop ECX to restore register
12. Return (stdcall: callee pops return address)

Parameters:
None - this is a standalone initialization function

Returns:
void - function returns no value, used for unit creation side effects

Special Cases:
- Magic constant 0x2b3b is the game context ID passed to command dispatcher
- Magic constant 0x2 is the unit type code passed to unit creation
- Magic constant 0x12 (18 decimal) is the unit class identifier
- Global 0x6fa65ed0 tracks active unit count (copied to 0x6fa64db8)
- Local variable unitClassAndType is stack-allocated (offset +0x8 from ESP after PUSH)

Stack Layout:
Offset  Size  Description
+0x0    0x4   Saved ECX (callee-saved)
+0x4    0x4   Return address
+0x8    0x4   unitClassAndType parameter (class/type structure)

0x6FA4C3F0.name: CreateDefaultGameUnit
0x6FA4C3F0.comment:
Creates a default game unit with dynamically selected type based on current game state.

Algorithm:
1. Call dispatch_command_handler() with magic value 0x1419 to retrieve unit name string
2. Store returned name pointer in ESI for later use
3. Check global game state variable at 0x6fa65ad4 for value 1
4. If state == 1, use magic value 0x141b to get default unit type via dispatch_command_handler()
5. If state != 1, use magic value 0x141a (fallback unit type) via dispatch_command_handler()
6. Load global unit counter from 0x6fa65ed0 into ECX (unit context)
7. Store the unit counter value at global address 0x6fa64db4 (unit context storage)
8. Call CreateAndInitializeUnit() with parameters:
   - Parameter 1 (ESI): name pointer from step 1
   - Parameter 2 (EAX): unit type value from step 4 or 5
   - Parameter 3: constant 1 (success indicator)
   - Parameter 4: constant 0xc (12 - unit class flag)
9. Return with cleanup (POP ESI, RET)

Parameters:
None - This is a parameterless initialization routine.

Returns:
void - No return value, but creates a unit as a side effect.

Special Cases:
- Magic values 0x1419, 0x141a, 0x141b are dispatch command codes for unit creation
- Global state at 0x6fa65ad4 controls unit type selection (acts as game mode flag)
- Unit counter at 0x6fa65ed0 incremented by CreateAndInitializeUnit()
- Context value 0x6fa64db4 set before unit creation (game session tracking)
- Always passes parameters (1, 0xc) to CreateAndInitializeUnit() indicating:
  - nUnitType = 1 (base unit type)
  - nUnitClass = 0xc (12 - character class identifier)

0x6FA4C430.name: InitializeBattleNetConnection
0x6FA4C430.comment:
Initializes BattleNet UI controls and configures realm selection.

Algorithm:
1. Check if initialization flag is set (DAT_6fa65ad4 == 1)
2. Initialize rendering system if initialization needed
3. Load current realm state from DAT_6fa65e78
4. If realm == -1: Handle disconnect state
   - Clear disconnect flags at offset 0x35d and 0x37d in game context
   - Dispatch callback for disconnection
   - Call virtual function at offset 0x10 in DAT_6fa656c4
   - Initialize BattleNet UI with callback InitializeGameSession
5. If realm == 0: Call FUN_6fa4e250 initialization routine
   - Initialize BattleNet UI with callback InitializeGameSession
6. If realm > 0: Configure preferred realm
   - Enqueue multiple game commands (0x7a, 0x94, 0x95, 0x69, 0x6b, 0x6c)
   - Search for preferred realm in string list "Diablo II"
   - If found: Return success (1)
   - If not found: Query gateway for available realms
     - Get realm name from gateway using virtual offset 0x98
     - Copy realm data to buffer at 0x6fa65758
     - Store new preferred realm using func_0x1018be10
     - Search again for preferred realm
     - If still not found: Use default realm (index 0x7fffffff)

Returns:
0: Initialization incomplete or BattleNet mode disabled
1: Initialization successful or configuration completed

Special Cases:
- BattleNet connection state stored in global DAT_6fa65e78
- Realm == -1 indicates disconnect/reconnect needed
- Realm == 0 indicates initial session setup
- Realm > 0 indicates active realm selection mode
- Multiple global buffers used for realm storage (0x6fa65758, 0x6fa5e204, 0x6fa5dc80)
- Virtual function dispatch used for gateway interaction through DAT_6fa656c4

Structure Layout:
Gateway context structure at DAT_6fa656c4:
  Offset 0x10: Virtual function pointer for cleanup/disconnect
  Offset 0x98: Virtual function pointer for gateway realm query

0x6FA4C610.name: ProcessInventoryInputEvent
0x6FA4C610.comment: Processes inventory input events and navigates slot selection.\"

0x6FA4C720.name: CreateAndInitializeCharacter
0x6FA4C720.signature: int CreateAndInitializeCharacter(char * pCharacterData, int pAttributePtr, uint dwExpansionData, uint dwSaveTime, uint dwSaveTimeHigh)
0x6FA4C720.comment:
Creates and initializes a new character unit with class, difficulty, and attribute data.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 0x350 bytes (848 bytes) of memory for character structure
2. Store save timestamp and expansion flag at offsets 0x340, 0x344, 0x348
3. Copy character data from pCharacterData parameter
4. Convert character name from ANSI to Unicode at offset 0x100
5. Validate realm name - if invalid, return 0
6. Extract and store character class (11 bytes) from pAttributePtr+2 into offset 0x300
7. Pad class data to 0x10 bytes with 0xFF fill value
8. Extract and store difficulty value, subtract 1, store at offset 0x320
9. Extract and store 11 bytes of attribute data from pAttributePtr+1 into offset 0x310
10. Pad attribute data to 0x10 bytes with 0xFF
11. Initialize attribute fields at offsets 0x322, 0x324, 0x328, 0x32A, 0x32E, 0x32F, 0x330
12. Apply special handling for expansion flag (0x4) and hardcore flag (0x8)
13. Call AllocateAndInitializeUnit to create actual unit object
14. If unit creation fails, create fallback unit with class 7 difficulty 5
15. Verify unit was created, abort if both attempts fail
16. Finalize unit item initialization and compute parameter values
17. Insert unit into global linked list (DAT_6fa65ec8) sorted by difficulty/timestamp
18. Increment global unit counter and render display
19. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
  pCharacterData: Pointer to character data (name, attributes, timestamps)
  pAttributePtr: Offset into character data with class/difficulty info
  dwExpansionData: Expansion flag (0 for base game)
  dwSaveTime: Timestamp (low 32 bits)
  dwSaveTimeHigh: Timestamp (high 32 bits)

Returns:
  1 (success) if character created and added to list
  0 (failure) if realm invalid or unit creation failed

Special Cases:
  - Invalid realm names return 0 immediately
  - Expansion + hardcore flags route to special classes
  - Attribute bytes 0xFF convert to 0
  - Fallback unit: class 7 difficulty 5
  - List sorted by difficulty, then timestamp"

0x6FA4CB00.name: ProcessAndInitializeCharacterData
0x6FA4CB00.signature: void ProcessAndInitializeCharacterData(uint expansionFlags, char * pConfigData, int enableCaching)
0x6FA4CB00.comment:
Processes and initializes character data from a configuration structure.

Algorithm:
1. Extract configuration parameters from pConfigData (max count, character type byte)
2. Validate expansion data using FindAndValidateD2ExpMpq()
3. If validation fails, initialize default unit via dispatch_command_handler()
4. Iterate through character count up to min(maxCharCount, configMaxCount)
5. For each character: extract expansion ID (if type 0x19), scan name string (null-terminated)
6. Scan path string (null-terminated), calculate offsets for each data region
7. Call CreateAndInitializeCharacter with extracted character data
8. On creation failure: decrement counter and call ClearCharacterCacheAndCleanup()
9. If caching enabled, call UpdateOrCreateCacheEntry with total data size
10. Check slot count threshold and set cache flag if condition met
11. Compare expansion counts and initialize expansion unit if needed
12. Call InitializeEntityCharacterAndRenderUI() for final setup

Parameters:
- expansionFlags: Expansion/mode flags passed to lower-level functions
- pConfigData: Pointer to character configuration structure containing character count, type, and character data
- enableCaching: Flag to enable caching of character data in cache system

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Handles type 0x19 (expansion character) which has additional expansion ID field at offset +9
- String scanning uses null-termination to find boundaries
- Maximum character count is limited by min(maxCharCount from config, maxAllowed)
- Cache update only occurs if enableCaching != 0
- Expansion unit creation triggered when configured count exceeds slot count

0x6FA4CC50.name: LoadSaveGameCharacters
0x6FA4CC50.comment:
Scans save game directory and loads all valid character save files.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize character load counter to zero
2. Build save game directory path using BuildSaveGamePath()
3. Format search pattern as "*.d2s" for save files
4. Open file search handle using FindFirstFileA()
5. For each file found:
   a. Extract filename before extension (copy until '.' or end)
   b. Validate filename meets criteria:
      - Length between 2-16 characters
      - Does not contain '-' as penultimate character
      - Does not start with '_'
      - Passes character validation (FUN_6fa4f190)
   c. If valid, call CreateAndInitializeCharacter() with filename and timestamps
   d. Increment character load counter
   e. Continue with FindNextFileA()
6. Close file search handle
7. Return 1 (success)

Returns:
  EAX=1: Function always returns success (1)

Special Cases:
  - Invalid/hidden files (starting with '_', or with '-' prefix) are skipped
  - Filenames with length < 2 or >= 16 are rejected
  - File timestamps (dwLowDateTime, dwHighDateTime) are passed to character creation
  - Character counter stored at address 0x6fa65eec

Structure Details:
  _WIN32_FIND_DATAA findFileData - Contains cFileName and ftLastWriteTime fields
  Save game path buffer - Local 1024-byte buffer formatted with save directory and pattern

0x6FA4CD70.name: InitializeGameSessionAndLoadZone
0x6FA4CD70.comment:
Initializes game session by searching for matching zone data and loading appropriate resources.

Iterates through a linked list of session configurations to find an entry matching the current string hash and within the active time window. Once found, loads zone data and initializes BattleNet UI. If no matching session is found or handler indicates failure, dispatches command and initializes UI with fallback path. Returns after setting error flags if initialization fails.

Algorithm:
1. Reset game state and audio configuration
2. Compute hash of context string for session matching
3. Get current system time for time-window validation
4. Load session list head pointer from global storage
5. Loop through linked list nodes:
   a. Check if current node pointer is null (end of list)
   b. Compare node hash with computed string hash
   c. Validate node timestamp against current time
   d. If match found, load zone data from node and initialize UI
   e. If match not found, advance to next node via offset +0xc
6. If no session found, call global state handler function
7. Test handler result - if success (0), dispatch command and initialize UI
8. If handler fails, set error flags and store context for later recovery
9. Return to caller

Parameters:
None - uses global state: DAT_6fa65ef4 (session list), DAT_6fa656c4 (handler vtable)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x6fa5c364: GetTickCount function address (time validation)
- Magic number 0x68: Offset into handler vtable for query function
- Magic number 0x6fa65eb8/0x6fa65ebc: Error state globals
- Session nodes are 16-byte linked list structures with offsets:
  +0x0: hash_string (dword)
  +0x4: zone_data_path (pointer)
  +0x8: expiry_time (dword)
  +0xc: next_node (pointer)

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name       | Type    | Description
-------|------|------------------|---------|--------------------
0x00   | 4    | hash_string      | dword   | Session identifier hash
0x04   | 4    | zone_data        | void*   | Pointer to zone file path
0x08   | 4    | expiry_time      | dword   | Session expiration timestamp
0x0C   | 4    | next_node        | Node*   | Next session node pointer

0x6FA4CE10.name: ProcessGameInitializationStateMachine
0x6FA4CE10.comment:
Manages game initialization through a multi-stage state machine.

This function coordinates the transition between four initialization states:
- State 1 (initial): Main game loop - processes character data and synchronizes game state
- State 2 (transitioning): Initialization phase - performs buffer encoding and module setup
- State 3 (module init): Module initialization - initializes game modules and configuration
- State 0 (running): Normal execution - handles ongoing game state updates

Algorithm:
1. Check initialization state stored in global DAT_6fa65eb8
2. If state != 1:
   - If state == 2: Execute initialization sequence with time-based UI updates (1000ms threshold)
     - Call ClearResourceState to reset current resources
     - Check game sync state via CheckGameSyncState
     - If sync complete (return 0): Initialize buffer encoding via InitializeBufferEncoding
     - If successful, transition to state 3 and call GetCurrentGameState/InitializeGameStartupSequence
     - Return 1 to continue processing
   - If state == 3: Execute module initialization sequence
     - Call ClearResourceState to reset resources
     - Call InitializeGameModule to set up game modules
     - Retrieve global game state via GetGlobalGameState
     - Transition to state 0 (normal operation)
     - If DAT_6fa65984 != 0, call SetLinkedListElementValue(4)
     - Process character data via ProcessAndInitializeCharacterData
     - Return 1 to continue
   - Otherwise: Return 1 (invalid state, no processing)
3. If state == 1 (main loop):
   - If DAT_6fa65984 != 0, call SetLinkedListElementValue(4)
   - Call SearchAndActivateListElement to activate list items
   - Compare character state against cached state at DAT_6fa65abc+0x229
   - If states match and no pending updates: Proceed to callback dispatch
   - If mismatch or pending updates: Jump to state transition (LAB_6fa4d02c)
   - Call DispatchCallbackOrVirtualFunction for event processing
   - Clear character data if no active character (pbVar1 == 0)
   - Otherwise: If DAT_6fa656c4 != 0, copy character state and call ProcessObjectStateUpdate
4. Transition to state 2 via DAT_6fa65eb8 = 2
5. Update time checkpoint via _DAT_6fa65ec0 = GetTickCount()
6. Return 1 to indicate continued processing

Parameters:
(void) - Function takes no parameters, operates on global game state

Returns:
int - Always returns 1 to indicate state machine should continue processing

Special Cases:
- Time-based UI refresh: When 1000ms elapsed, triggers UI update via dispatch_command_handler(4,0,0)
- Character comparison uses byte-by-byte string comparison to detect state changes
- If no query object available (DAT_6fa656c4 == 0), skips ProcessObjectStateUpdate
- If query result has type 8, skips state copy operations (protection check)
- State 0 (normal): Continues looping without state change until next event

Global Dependencies:
DAT_6fa65eb8 - Current initialization state (0=running, 1=main, 2=init, 3=modInit)
DAT_6fa65ec0 - Last time checkpoint for 1000ms refresh throttle
DAT_6fa65ebc - Current character/entity pointer
DAT_6fa65abc - Game state structure base (contains +0x229 state cache, +0xd1 flags)
DAT_6fa65984 - List element state flag
DAT_6fa65e80 - Output state flag (cleared each frame)
DAT_6fa656c4 - Query object factory/cache
DAT_6fa656fc - List element context

0x6FA4D050.name: InitializeGameStateAndRenderUI
0x6FA4D050.comment:
Initializes game state and renders the UI based on game mode.

Algorithm:
1. Clear the screen rendering flag (DAT_6fa65ee4 = 0)
2. Check the game state variable (DAT_6fa65ad4)
3. If state is 1 (new game initialization):
   - Clear all resource state
   - Render text box with unicode conversion (parameter 0)
   - Initialize game session and load current zone
   - Initialize entity, character, and render UI
   - Render entity display on screen
   - Return
4. If state is 0, 2, or 3 (game load/resume modes):
   - Reset game screenshots and audio subsystem
   - Validate Diablo II expansion MPQ files
   - If MPQ validation fails (result == 0), create default unit
   - Load saved game character data
5. Initialize entity, character, and render UI
6. Render entity display on screen

Parameters:
- (implicit in EDI) Game context pointer or session data

Returns:
- void

Special Cases:
- State value 1 represents new game initialization
- States 0, 2, 3 represent different load/resume scenarios
- If FindAndValidateD2ExpMpq() returns 0, creates default unit as fallback
- All paths converge to render UI at completion

0x6FA4D0D0.name: JoinGameWithSelectedCharacter
0x6FA4D0D0.comment:
Joins game with the selected character and connects to the specified realm.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieves the selected character name from a linked list
2. Converts character name from Unicode to UTF-8 format
3. Initializes game state and rendering UI with loaded character
4. Cleans up previous game resources
5. Attempts to validate/initialize realm connection
6. If validation succeeds, copies character data and initiates connection to preferred realm
7. Resets game state and UI controls
8. Returns success status

Parameters:
None - operates on global game state and selected character

Returns:
1 (always returns success; actual connection result stored in global state)

Special Cases:
- Connection failure silently skipped; function always returns 1
- Magic value 0x7fffffff passed to memory copy (max size)
- Realm connection handled by external function at 0x1018be10

0x6FA4D140.name: InitializeGameEngine
0x6FA4D140.comment:
Initializes the game engine state and rendering subsystem.

Algorithm:
1. Load game state context pointer into EAX from address 0x6fa65758
2. Call InitializeGameStateAndRenderUI() with the context as implicit this pointer
3. Call ResetGameStateAndUIControls() to reset game state and UI elements
4. Return 1 (success indicator)

Parameters:
Implicit this pointer in ECX - Game engine context structure

Returns:
1 - Initialization successful

Notes:
This function is the primary entry point for game engine initialization, 
orchestrating both the render pipeline setup and game state reset. The context 
pointer at 0x6fa65758 likely points to a global game engine or manager structure.

0x6FA4D160.name: InitializeGameSessionWithUI
0x6FA4D160.comment:
Initializes the complete game session with UI and BattleNet connection.

Algorithm:
1. Clear and reset all game UI controls and resources
2. Initialize palette file (Sky.pal) for color tables
3. Clear critical game state variables (frame counter, sprite data, etc)
4. Fill command buffer (0x40 slots) with 8 ProcessGameCommand calls from 8 resource addresses
5. Initialize MPQ (game archive) file validation and setup
6. Process each MPQ module (8 total) with FindAndValidateD2ExpMpq, calculate screen positions
7. Store base command result and validate BattleNet connection status
8. Branch on game mode:
   - Mode 1 (single player): Clear resources, load initial characters
   - Mode 0/2/3 (multiplayer): Reset audio, load save game characters
9. Initialize character entities and render main game screen
10. Process extra units if entity count > 8
11. Check audio option flag and enable music system if needed
12. Final cleanup and return on success, or abort with error on failure

Returns:
void - No return value, function handles all results through global state variables

Special Cases:
- Command buffer overflow: If any ProcessGameCommand causes buffer to exceed 0x40 slots, function terminates with error
- MPQ validation loop: Iterates 8 times with stride +0x30, checks FindAndValidateD2ExpMpq result
- Screen position calculation: (loopIndex / 2) * 0x5d + 0xb2 (spacing formula for UI elements)
- Game mode check: DAT_6fa65ad4 == 1 (single player), == 0/2/3 (multiplayer/other modes)
- Character load sentinel: dispatch_command_handler calls return character name/path pointers
- Audio flag check: GetAudioOptionFlag determines if music system should be initialized

0x6FA4D5D0.name: InitializeGameWorld
0x6FA4D5D0.comment:
Initialize game world and load expansion data

Initializes core game systems including palette loading, game state setup,
expansion mode configuration, command processing, and realm data loading.
Handles both expansion 1 and standard modes with different initialization
paths and command sequences.

Algorithm:
1. Validate and load expansion MPQ file (FindAndValidateD2ExpMpq)
2. If validation fails, initialize Battle.Net UI and return early
3. Clear game UI controls and set initial game state
4. Load sky palette file (s_palette_sky_pal_pl2)
5. Check expansion mode flag (DAT_6fa65ad4)
   - If mode -1 or 0: Initialize rendering and Battle.Net controls, return
   - If mode 1: Continue with expansion 1 initialization
   - Otherwise: Initialize expansion 0 (standard) mode
6. Initialize game state variables (DAT_6fa65eb0 through DAT_6fa65edc to 0/1)
7. Setup command queue base pointers and offset values
8. Clear command result buffer and flag arrays
9. Set initial command list configuration (4 for expansion 1, 5 for standard)
10. Loop: Process expansion commands with resource data entries (0x30 bytes each)
11. Validate command count does not exceed 0x40 (64 max)
12. Append additional expansion-specific commands to queue
13. Load realm data from preference file (s_Preferred_Realm)
14. Search realm in configured list
15. If realm found: Copy realm name from gateway
16. If realm not found: Use default realm from configuration or error code 0x1143
17. Write realm preference back to config file
18. Call audio system and UI initialization
19. If connection fails: Display error message and exit with code -1

Parameters:
None - Uses static game configuration global variables

Returns:
void - Function handles all errors internally via CleanupAndAbort if
connection to Battle.Net fails (error code 0x624 or 0x1143)

Special Cases:
- MPQ file validation failure triggers early exit via InitializeGameSessionWithUI
- Expansion mode -1 and 0 have identical initialization and early return
- Command buffer limit 0x40 triggers error with code 0x624 if exceeded
- Null realm pointer returns error code 0x1143
- All game configuration is driven by global variables (DAT_6fa65ad4 mode flag)
- SetExpansionMode called twice in each loop iteration (compiler optimization)
- Magic numbers: 0xf6/0x99 base resource IDs, 0x5d offset multiplier per iteration
- Resource data entries are 0x30 (48) bytes, contain command information

0x6FA4DB60.name: ProcessAnimationFrame
0x6FA4DB60.comment:
Searches linked list of animation nodes and updates animation frame state.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize counter to zero and get first animation node from global
2. Loop through animation node linked list (offset +0x34c to next)
3. Compare counter with global index (DAT_6fa64db0) to find target node
4. When target found, check if Unicode name at +0x100 is valid
5. Convert Unicode name to Windows format using buffer
6. Call UpdateAnimationFrame to process animation
7. If update returns zero, dispatch command handler and initialize UI
8. If update returns non-zero, increment frame counter and continue
9. Otherwise finalize animation and return success

Parameters:
None (uses global animation context)

Returns:
0 - Animation list is empty or animation not found
1 - Animation frame processed successfully

Special Cases:
- Empty animation list returns 0
- Invalid Unicode name at offset +0x100 skips processing
- Animation update failure (non-zero return) triggers command dispatch and UI init
- Uses static buffer (256 bytes) for Unicode conversion

Structure Layout:
Animation node layout (from assembly):
Offset  Size  Field Name        Type      Description
+0x100  2     unicodeName       Unicode   Unicode string for animation name
+0x34c  4     nextNode          ptr       Pointer to next animation in linked list

0x6FA4DC50.name: InitializeMultiplayerGameSession
0x6FA4DC50.comment:
Initialize a multiplayer game session by validating the player's Unicode character name and applying game state updates. Manages the session linked list lookup, validates expansion availability, and configures UI components.

Algorithm:
1. Verify Diablo II expansion is available via FindAndValidateD2ExpMpq()
2. Iterate through game state linked list (0x6fa65ec8) to find matching session index (0x6fa64db0)
3. Check if session is already active using status flag at offset 0x324 (bit 0x20)
4. If active, return early; if inactive, proceed to validation
5. Check if player Unicode name exists at offset 0x100 (non-zero pointer with non-empty string)
6. If name missing, initialize new player session via FUN_6fa4f030() and setup UI
7. If name present, convert Unicode to Windows format into buffer [ESP+0x10]
8. Call ValidateAndApplyGameStateUpdate() to validate game state
9. If validation fails, check current game state via GetCurrentGameState()
10. If state is 0x7b, initialize two 512-element Unicode buffers, convert player name, format command string, and setup UI
11. Otherwise, setup UI with standard initialization callback and return
12. If validation succeeds, mark session active (set flag 0x20 at offset 0x324), render display, destroy UI controls
13. Call ModifyObjectBitfield() before returning success code 0x1

Parameters:
None - operates on global game state pointers

Returns:
1 on success (always returns 1 in all code paths)

Special Cases:
- Magic offset 0x324: Player session status flags (bit 0x20 = active)
- Magic offset 0x100: Unicode character name pointer
- Magic offset 0x34c: Next player session in linked list
- State 0x7b: Special initialization with name formatting and command dispatch
- 0x6fa65ec8: Global head pointer to game state list
- 0x6fa64db0: Global current session index
- 0x6fa65eac: Session counter reset flag

Structure Layout:
Game state structure accessed via ESI:
  Offset  Size  Field          Type       Description
  0x100   4     pName          Unicode*   Player character name (Unicode string)
  0x324   1     flags          byte       Status flags (bit 0x20 = active)
  0x34c   4     pNext          GameState* Pointer to next session in linked list"

0x6FA4DE20.name: ProcessSelectedEntityCommand
0x6FA4DE20.comment:
Processes a command for the selected entity/unit by finding it in the linked list and executing the command.

Algorithm
1. Load the selected entity index from global DAT_6fa64db0 and check if it is -1 (invalid)
2. If invalid, return immediately without processing
3. Load the entity list base pointer from DAT_6fa65ec8
4. Validate that the entity list is not null
5. Initialize loop counter to 0 and iterate through linked list
6. For each iteration, load next entity pointer from offset +0x34c (next node link)
7. Compare loop counter with target index; if equal, exit loop
8. If entity pointer is null, return without processing (invalid entity)
9. Once target entity found, write commandByte to game state at DAT_6fa65abc + 0x20c
10. Destroy all UI controls to refresh the interface
11. Convert entity's Unicode name (at offset +0x100) to Windows ANSI string
12. Execute game command by reading entity's byte at offset +0x320 and calling ProcessGameCommand with command and converted name
13. Return from function

Parameters
commandByte (byte) - Command code to execute on the selected entity; written to game state at offset 0x20c

Returns
void - No return value; modifies game state and UI through side effects

Special Cases
- If global DAT_6fa64db0 is -1, function returns immediately (no entity selected)
- If entity list DAT_6fa65ec8 is null, function returns immediately (no entities available)
- If loop counter exceeds available entities before finding match, function returns
- If entity pointer becomes null during iteration, function returns

Entity Structure Layout (accessed via ESI)
Offset 0x100 - Unicode name string pointer (converted to Windows text)
Offset 0x320 - Command byte field (extracted and passed to ProcessGameCommand)
Offset 0x34c - Next entity pointer (linked list traversal)

0x6FA4DEC0.name: ProcessGameStateAndInitialize
0x6FA4DEC0.comment:
Processes game state transitions and initializes game components based on current mode.

ALGORITHM:
1. Load game state and config pointers from global data
2. Check if game is already initialized (DAT_6fa65eac); return if true
3. Check if game state matches expected value (DAT_6fa64db0 vs DAT_6fa64db4)
   - If states match: Initialize game commands if mode is 1 and not already initialized
   - Otherwise: Continue to state-specific processing
4. Validate current state index against reserved value (-1); return if invalid
5. If current state index is not -1:
   - Traverse state list (DAT_6fa65ec8) by offset 0x34c to find matching state object
   - Return 1 if state object not found in list
6. Copy state data from source object to destination:
   - If game mode is 1 or 3: Copy 11 DWORDs from state offsets 0x300-0x318 to dest 0x39d-0x3b9
   - Copy byte flags and word settings from state offsets 0x322-0x324
7. Validate expansion MPQ if bit 0x20 set in state flags; return 0 if validation fails
8. Check for BattleNet initialization (bits 0x4 and 0x8 set):
   - If game mode is 0 or 2: Initialize BattleNet UI with command dispatcher
9. Check for command handler initialization (difficulty level 3-5 in bits 8-12):
   - If mode is 0 or (mode is 2 and config value at 0x15 is 8): Initialize game command handlers
10. Convert game command string from Unicode to Windows format
11. Process game command via ProcessGameCommand with command type and converted string
12. Return 1 (success)

PARAMETERS:
None

RETURNS:
int - Status code (1 for success/continue, 0 for validation failure)

0x6FA4E140.name: ValidateGameEntityAndInitializeState
0x6FA4E140.comment:
Validates a game entity against known lists and initializes game state if conditions are met.

ALGORITHM:
1. Check if game state is already initialized (DAT_6fa65984); return 1 if true
2. Load current state value and initialize search index to 0
3. Validate entity ID (first param) against two global entity lists:
   - Loop through indices 0 to DAT_6fa64dbc
   - Check if entity matches DAT_6fa65858[index] or DAT_6fa65734[index]
   - Exit loop early if match found or validation fails
4. Validate entity index is within bounds (DAT_6fa65ed4 + index <= DAT_6fa65ed0)
   - Return 0 if bounds check fails
5. Update DAT_6fa64db0 with calculated value (DAT_6fa65ed4 + index)
   - Set to -1 if DAT_6fa65ed0 < 1
6. Check if special mode 0x201 is active (param[1] == 0x201):
   - If yes: Get current tick count and validate timing/state conditions
   - If current state unchanged and time delta < 500ms: call ProcessGameStateAndInitialize()
   - Otherwise: Update tick count and call InitializeEntityCharacterAndRenderUI()
   - If no: Always call InitializeEntityCharacterAndRenderUI()
7. Return status code from initialization function

PARAMETERS:
pEntityId (int *): Pointer to entity identifier to validate against game entity lists

RETURNS:
int: 1 for success/initialization performed, 0 if entity validation or bounds check fails

SPECIAL CASES:
- Early return (1) if game already initialized (DAT_6fa65984 != 0)
- Entity validation timeout: 500ms throttle via GetTickCount() prevents rapid reinitializations
- State value -1 indicates resource clearing state (DAT_6fa65ed0 < 1)
- Mode 0x201 triggers state-aware initialization path; other modes use standard UI initialization

GLOBAL STATE DEPENDENCIES:
DAT_6fa65984: Game initialized flag
DAT_6fa64db0: Current state value
DAT_6fa64dbc: Entity list count
DAT_6fa65858: Primary entity list address
DAT_6fa65734: Secondary entity list address
DAT_6fa65ed0: Max entity count
DAT_6fa65ed4: Entity base offset
DAT_6fa65ef8: Last tick count timestamp

0x6FA4E220.name: ExecuteEntityCommand2
0x6FA4E220.comment:
Executes command type 2 on the currently selected entity.

This is a wrapper function that invokes ProcessSelectedEntityCommand with a hardcoded command byte of 2. Command 2 typically represents a specific game action for the selected entity (such as selection confirmation or a predefined action).

Algorithm
1. Push command byte 2 onto stack as parameter
2. Call ProcessSelectedEntityCommand(2) to process the command on selected entity
3. Move return value 1 (success) into EAX register
4. Return to caller with RET 0x4 (callee cleanup)

Parameters
None - function takes no parameters; uses hardcoded command byte 2

Returns
int - Returns 1 to indicate successful command execution/queuing

Special Cases
- Function always succeeds (returns 1) regardless of whether entity selection is valid
- Actual command processing and validation happens in ProcessSelectedEntityCommand
- If no entity is selected, ProcessSelectedEntityCommand handles the validation

0x6FA4E250.name: DisconnectFromBattleNet
0x6FA4E250.comment:
Initiates disconnection from BattleNet server by clearing session state and invoking cleanup callbacks.

Algorithm:
1. Load the global BattleNet connection state pointer (DAT_6fa656c4)
2. Check if the connection state exists (non-zero)
3. If no active connection, return immediately (early exit)
4. If connection exists:
   a. Set global disconnect flag (DAT_6fa65eb0 = 1) to signal disconnection in progress
   b. Clear connection state flags at offset +0x35d (likely connection active flag)
   c. Clear additional state flag at offset +0x37d (likely session validation flag)
   d. Output debug message "Disconnect_from_BNET" for logging/debugging
   e. Call DispatchCallbackOrVirtualFunction to invoke pending callbacks
   f. Invoke virtual function through connection state vtable at offset +0x10
   g. Return from function

Parameters:
None - uses global state variables for connection management

Returns:
void - Function performs state cleanup and callback dispatch but returns no value

Special Cases:
- If DAT_6fa656c4 is null, function returns immediately without any cleanup
- The indirect jump at 0x6fa4e28b invokes a virtual function from the connection object's vtable
- Offset 0x35d appears to be a connection active/validation flag
- Offset 0x37d appears to be an additional session state flag

0x6FA4E2A0.name: IsShutdownRequested
0x6FA4E2A0.comment:
Queries the current shutdown/exit requested flag
Returns the value of the global shutdown flag (0x6fa65ea0) which indicates whether the application should shut down or exit the current game state.

Algorithm:
1. Load the 32-bit value from global address 0x6fa65ea0 into EAX
2. Return the loaded value to caller

Returns:
- Non-zero (true) if shutdown/exit is requested
- Zero (false) if shutdown/exit is not requested

Special Cases:
- This flag is set by IsShutdownRequested_Set (0x6fa4e2c0) and ClearShutdownFlag (0x6fa4e2b0)
- Used by game loop control functions to determine when to exit processing
- Global flag controls UI cleanup and resource deallocation

0x6FA4E2B0.name: ClearShutdownFlag
0x6FA4E2B0.comment:
Clears the global shutdown/exit requested flag to allow game processing to continue.

Algorithm:
1. Write 0 to global address 0x6fa65ea0 to clear the shutdown flag
2. Return to caller

Returns:
- void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- This flag is checked by game loop control functions to determine when to exit
- Used in conjunction with IsShutdownRequested() reader and SetShutdownFlag() writer
- Critical for game session control and UI cleanup procedures

0x6FA4E2C0.name: SetGameInitializationFlag
0x6FA4E2C0.comment:
Sets the global game initialization flag to indicate that the game engine has completed its startup sequence.

Algorithm:
1. Set the global initializationFlag variable to 1 (true)
2. Return to caller

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
This function is called during game startup to signal that initialization is complete. The initializationFlag is used by other game functions to check if the engine is ready.

0x6FA4E2D0.name: ValidateNetworkInitializationAndCleanup
0x6FA4E2D0.comment:
Validates network/Battle.Net initialization state and performs cleanup.

Algorithm:
1. Load initialization flag from DAT_6fa656c0
2. Test if flag is zero (not yet initialized)
3. If uninitialized (EQ path):
   a. Call GetReturnAddress(0x77) to get stack frame return address
   b. Call CleanupAndAbort with error message "Can't connect to Battle.Net"
   c. Call _exit(-1) to terminate process (non-returning)
4. If already initialized (JNZ path):
   a. Call InitializeCleanupForEntryPoint to register cleanup handlers
   b. Clear initialization flag at DAT_6fa656c0 = 0
   c. Clear related global at DAT_6fa656c4 = 0
   d. Return to caller

Parameters:
None (void function, __stdcall calling convention)

Returns:
void - Function either returns normally (if initialized) or terminates process

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x77 passed to GetReturnAddress likely encodes stack frame depth
- Function does NOT return if initialization check fails (_exit is non-returning)
- Two global DWORDs must be cleared atomically before returning
- Error message comes from hardcoded string at 0x6fa5e256 with offset +0x2e

0x6FA4E320.name: InitializeBattleNetClient
0x6FA4E320.comment:
Initialize Battle.Net client connection by loading Bnclient.dll and obtaining interface pointer.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that pGameState pointer is not NULL; if NULL, call cleanup and abort
2. Check if Battle.Net client is already initialized at offset +0x221
3. If not initialized:
   a. Load Bnclient.dll using LoadLibraryA
   b. If load fails, get error code via GetLastError, format error message, show MessageBox, return 0
   c. Call GetProcAddress to locate QueryInterface function in loaded DLL
   d. If QueryInterface not found, get error code, format error message, show MessageBox, return 0
   e. Call QueryInterface function to obtain interface pointer
   f. Store interface pointer in two locations: global DAT_6fa656c4 and pGameState[0x221]
   g. Call interface initialization method (dereference pointer at offset 0)
4. Return 1 to indicate success

Parameters:
  pGameState: Pointer to game state structure containing Battle.Net initialization flag at offset +0x221

Returns:
  1 - Battle.Net client successfully initialized or already initialized
  0 - Failed to load Bnclient.dll or QueryInterface function

Special Cases:
  - Function uses implicit ECX register (thiscall convention) for pGameState
  - If pGameState is NULL, function calls cleanup/abort (never returns normally)
  - Error messages shown to user via MessageBox for DLL load and QueryInterface failures
  - Magic offset 0x221 indicates specific field in game state structure

0x6FA4E400.name: CheckAndInitializeRenderingState
0x6FA4E400.comment:
Checks and initializes the rendering state based on system conditions.

Algorithm:
1. Call virtual function at offset 0xa0 to check rendering state
2. If result is non-zero, initialize rendering system
3. Check if initialization flag is zero and call virtual function at offset 0x68
4. If that function returns non-zero AND game execution is disabled, return 1
5. Call virtual function at offset 0x10 (cleanup/reset function)
6. Call final rendering initialization
7. Return 1 (success status)

Parameters:
(implicit) - No explicit parameters, operates on global game state

Returns:
int - Always returns 1 (success status)

Special Cases:
- Early exit when initialization flag (0x6fa65ea0) is already set
- Conditional execution based on game execution enabled flag (0x6fa65e60)
- Virtual function calls through vtable at 0x6fa656c4
- Magic values: offsets 0xa0, 0x68, 0x10 are vtable function pointers

0x6FA4E4A0.name: InitializeGameState
0x6FA4E4A0.comment:
Initialize game state and rendering systems

Algorithm:
1. Call first state management function from vtable at DAT_6fa656c4 + 0xc
2. If result is non-zero, initialize rendering state
3. Check if initialization flag (DAT_6fa65ea0) is zero
4. If flag is zero and second vtable function (DAT_6fa656c4 + 0x68) returns non-zero
5. Check if game execution is disabled (g_gameExecutionEnabled == 0)
6. If game execution is disabled, call rendering initialization
7. Return success status (1)

Returns:
1 on success

Special Cases:
- Function always returns 1 regardless of initialization success
- Conditional rendering initialization based on state flags
- Uses function pointers from game state vtable

0x6FA4E4E0.name: UpdateRenderingState
0x6FA4E4E0.comment:
Conditionally updates rendering state based on game status and rendering flags.
Checks if the game status is 0x65 (likely 'e' for an error or escape state) and whether 
rendering is enabled. If status != 0x65 and rendering is disabled, processes and renders 
scaled frame text. Otherwise initializes the rendering state.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve current game status from the status callback at offset 0x4c of global state
2. Compare status value against sentinel 0x65
3. If status equals 0x65, skip to rendering initialization
4. If status != 0x65, check if rendering is disabled (DAT_6fa65294 == 0)
5. If rendering disabled, call ProcessAndRenderScaledFrameText to render text
6. Otherwise call InitializeRenderingState to initialize rendering
7. Return success code (1)

Returns:
1 - Always returns 1 indicating successful completion

Special Cases:
0x65 - Sentinel value indicating special game state (possibly escape/menu state)
DAT_6fa65294 - Global flag controlling rendering enabled/disabled state (0=disabled, non-zero=enabled)

0x6FA4E510.name: ProcessGameUICommand
0x6FA4E510.comment:
Processes game UI initialization commands and dispatches to appropriate handlers.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate three Unicode string buffers (512 chars each = 2048 bytes total)
2. Extract command ID from pCommandRecord->dwCommandId (EDI+0x0)
3. Perform switch dispatch on command ID (cases 0x0 through 0x1b)
4. For command-specific cases: set configStringId and handlerType flags
5. For cases 6/10 (custom UI): validate param at pCommandRecord->pCustomData (EDI+0x4)
6. Retrieve three configuration strings via dispatch_command_handler() into buffers
7. Dispatch to appropriate handler based on handlerType:
   - Type 0: InitializeBattleNetUIControls(primary, callback, 1)
   - Type 1: InitializeUIWithGameCommands(tertiary, primary, callback)
   - Type 2: InitializeUIControlsWithParameters(tertiary, primary, secondary, callback)
8. If shouldDispatchCallback: call DispatchCallbackOrVirtualFunction and invoke virtual at offset +0x10
9. Return 0

Parameters:
- pCommandRecord: Pointer to command structure containing:
  - Offset +0x0: dwCommandId (UI initialization command type, range 0-27)
  - Offset +0x4: pCustomData (optional pointer for custom UI data, NULL for most commands)

Returns:
- 0 on all paths (void return encoded as int)

Special Cases:
- Command 0x1b (31): Special handling for UTF8 conversion with dispatch integration
- Cases 6/10 (BattleNet UI): Validate pCustomData is not NULL before processing
- Invalid command: Falls through to default case, returns without initialization
- Magic numbers: 0x147c-0x1481 are string resource IDs, 0x2bb0-0x2bb2 for special cases

Callback Invocation:
- Conditional callback dispatch based on shouldDispatchCallback flag (set false for some command groups)
- Virtual function invoked from DAT_6fa656c4 at offset +0x10 (likely vtable entry)

0x6FA4EA90.name: DispatchGameUICommand
0x6FA4EA90.comment:
Dispatches a game UI command by preparing registers and calling the command processor.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 8 bytes on stack for command buffer (2 DWORDs)
2. Store EAX (command code) at [ESP + 4] offset
3. Store ECX (parameter) at [ESP] offset
4. Call ProcessGameUICommand with buffer address in ECX
5. Clean up stack and return

Parameters:
- EAX (implicit): Command code (0x14-0x17, etc.) indicating which UI action to process
- ECX (implicit): Parameter value, typically 0 (cleared with XOR before call)

Returns:
- void: No return value, function is a void wrapper

Special Cases:
- Function is called multiple times from FUN_6fa4eab0 with different command codes in EAX
- ECX is always cleared (XOR ECX,ECX) before each call
- Stack buffer provides temporary storage for command parameters
- Calling convention is __stdcall (RET after ADD ESP,0x8)

Structure Layout:
Stack buffer layout (8 bytes total):
  Offset  Size  Field Name     Type  Description
  +0      4     param1         dword Parameter value (ECX)
  +4      4     commandCode    dword Command code (EAX)

0x6FA4EAB0.name: DispatchGameCommand
0x6FA4EAB0.comment:
Main game command dispatcher and state machine orchestrator.

Manages game initialization, UI command processing, and state transitions based on
command codes and execution context. Handles BattleNet UI initialization, game session
management, and command dispatch for various game modes.

Algorithm:
1. Check if game engine is initialized (call function ptr at DAT_6fa656c4+0x68)
2. If not initialized, dispatch BattleNet UI initialization and exit
3. If already started (DAT_6fa65ea4 != 0), return early
4. Initialize game UI subsystem and begin command processing
5. Branch on commandCode parameter:
   - commandCode == 0: Enter alternate command path with additional state checking
   - commandCode != 0: Process specific command dispatch table (codes 2-8)
6. Clear game state registers (offsets +0xa1 to +0xb5, 6 dwords total)
7. Queue final rendering and check for error conditions
8. If post-game initialization enabled, execute callback dispatcher and session cleanup
9. Send final command code 0x12 to game UI command processor

Parameters:
  int commandCode - Game state/command identifier (0=init, 1=resume, 2-8=game modes)
  int param2 - Execution flag or additional command parameter

Returns:
  int - Status code (0=success/continue, 1=initialized/complete)

Special Cases:
  * Magic numbers: 0x12 = final init command, 0x68/0x28/0x60 = function dispatch offsets
  * State registers cleared at offsets +0xa1,+0xa5,+0xa9,+0xad,+0xb1,+0xb5 from base
  * Early exit if DAT_6fa65ea4 is already set (prevents double initialization)
  * Multiple rendering queue callbacks at different code paths (0x6fa4e450, 0x6fa4e400, etc)
  * Unaffected register EDI contains base context pointer for state structure access

0x6FA4EE10.name: ProcessGameInitialization
0x6FA4EE10.comment:
Manages game initialization and connection state transitions

Algorithm:
1. Check if game object at 0x6fa656c4 is initialized; return 0 if not
2. Verify no reentrant call by checking flag at 0x6fa65ea8; abort if already in progress
3. Set reentrance guard flag (0x6fa65ea8=1) and initialization flag (0x6fa65eb0=1)
4. Call virtual function at +0x10 offset on game object to perform initial callback
5. If callback returns 0: reset state, process UI command at [ESP+0x4], return result
6. If callback succeeds: set flag 0x6fa65ea4=0, call FUN_6fa4fc40, process rendering queue
7. Check initialization state flag (0x6fa65294):
   - If not initialized: check game state at +0x4c offset
   - If state != 0x66: initialize command processor, check state again
   - If state == 0x65: process character data from +0x48 offset
   - If no result: write registry values, initialize session, terminate process
   - If has result: process UI command with result code 0x12
8. If already initialized: set flag 0x6fa65be0=1, destroy UI controls, return 0
9. Handle various error conditions with cleanup and virtual function calls

Return Values:
- 0: Normal success or uninitialized state
- 1: Game state check true (negative result converted)
- UI command result: Varies by state path

Global State Modified:
- 0x6fa65ea8: Reentrance flag (1 during processing, 0 on exit)
- 0x6fa65eb0: Initialization flag
- 0x6fa65294: State flag
- 0x6fa65ea4, 0x6fa65be0: State tracking flags
- Registry writes to "Diablo II" keys

Special Cases:
- Reentrance protection: Function aborts with exit(-1) if already processing
- Multiple error paths with cleanup
- Virtual function dispatch pattern (indirect calls via +0x10, +0x4c, +0x48, +0x28, +0x68)
- State machine with 5+ branches based on game initialization state

0x6FA4F030.name: ValidateAndProcessSaveFile
0x6FA4F030.comment:
Validates and processes a save game file by checking header integrity and file size bounds.

Algorithm:
1. Build the save game file path based on game mode
2. Format the filename using game mode parameter
3. Create/open the save file with exclusive access
4. Return error if file creation fails
5. Read first 0x2000 bytes of file data
6. Validate bytes read >= 8 bytes
7. Check magic number at offset 0x604 (0xaa55aa55)
8. Get header size from offset 0x608
9. For files with 0x82-0x2000 bytes: set 0x20 flag, seek to start, write processed data
10. For files with > 0x14f bytes: set 0x20 flag, compute checksum, seek to start, write
11. Write result back to file
12. Close file and return write result or 0 on error

Parameters:
  gameMode (undefined4): Game mode identifier used to construct save file path

Returns:
  undefined4: Result from WriteFileThunk on success, 0 on validation failure

Special Cases:
  - Files smaller than 8 bytes fail validation
  - Header magic number must match 0xaa55aa55
  - Header size field must be <= 0x5b or > 0x14f
  - File size bounds checked: 0x82 for small files, 0x14f for large files
  - Checksum computation triggered for large files > 0x14f bytes

0x6FA4F190.name: LoadSaveGameCharacter
0x6FA4F190.comment:
Loads a save game character file and formats character data for processing.

Algorithm:
1. Validate character name parameter is not empty
2. Build the save game file path using character index and name
3. Open the save game file for reading
4. Read 0x2000 bytes (8KB) of save game data
5. Validate magic number (0xaa55aa55) confirming valid save format
6. Check version offset field (versionOffset) to determine data layout
7. If versionOffset < 0x5c: copy class data from lower version offsets (+0x636 to +0x646)
8. If versionOffset >= 0x5c and <= 0x60: copy class data from higher version offsets (+0x698 to +0x6a8)
9. Verify file size matches expected bytes for detected version
10. Encode character class ID using EncodeValueAsSignedBytes
11. Copy class name from source (11 bytes) or use default class names
12. Copy second character data block (11 bytes) with experience/mode bytes
13. Encode experience value and padding bytes
14. Set terminator bytes (0xff 0xff 0xff 0x00)
15. Close save game file
16. Return 1 on success, 0 on any validation failure

Parameters:
  characterIndex: Character slot number (0-N) to identify which character file
  characterName: Character name string to construct save game filename

Returns:
  1 if character data successfully loaded and formatted
  0 if file not found, validation failed, or format error detected

Special Cases:
  - Empty character name triggers error handler
  - Version offset determines data layout (two possible memory locations)
  - Default class names used if class name field is null
  - File must be exactly 0x2000 bytes and contain valid magic number

0x6FA4F3A0.name: DeleteFilesInDirectory
0x6FA4F3A0.comment:
Deletes all non-directory files matching a pattern in the save game directory.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that filePattern parameter is not empty
2. Build the save game directory base path
3. If basePath exists and is not empty, format directory path and create directories recursively
4. Format the full search pattern combining directory and file pattern
5. Call FindFirstFileA to start searching for files
6. Loop through all matching files with FindNextFileA:
   a. Format the full file path for current match
   b. Get file attributes to determine if it's a directory
   c. If it's a directory (FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DIRECTORY = 0x10), skip to next file
   d. If it's a regular file, call DeleteFileA to remove it
   e. If FindNextFileA returns 0 (no more files), exit cleanly
   f. If DeleteFileA returns 0 (failure), exit with error
7. Return after all files processed or on first error

Parameters:
- filePattern (ECX): File search pattern (e.g., "*.sav")
- basePath (EAX): Base directory path; NULL or empty uses default

Returns:
- void

Special Cases:
- Empty filePattern: calls CleanupAndAbort with error
- NULL/empty basePath: skips directory creation
- INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE: exits silently
- FindNextFileA = 0: exits silently (no more files)
- DeleteFileA = 0: exits silently (permission denied)

0x6FA4F4F0.name: WriteSaveGameFile
0x6FA4F4F0.comment:
Writes the current game state to a save game file with checksum validation.

Algorithm:
1. Allocate 1528 bytes on stack for path and data buffers
2. Construct save game file path via BuildSaveGamePath()
3. Format save game filename using sprintf with state ID parameter
4. Call CreateFileWrapper to create/open file (returns 0 on failure)
5. Check file handle: if 0, return 0 (failure), otherwise continue
6. Compute CRC32 checksum of 335-byte (0x14f) game state buffer at 0x6fa65570
7. Store computed checksum at global address 0x6fa6557c
8. Write 335 bytes of file header with WriteFileThunk
9. Close file handle with CloseResourceHandle
10. Return 1 (success)

Parameters:
nGameStateId: Game state identifier or slot index for save file naming

Returns:
1 if file was successfully written and closed
0 if file creation failed

Special Cases:
- Buffer size is fixed at 335 bytes (0x14f) for save game data
- Checksum computation required before file write
- File handle validation (non-zero check) determines success/failure path
- Stack frame 0x5f8 (1528 bytes) includes 1024-byte buffer + 500-byte path + 4-byte checksum

Structure Layout:
Save game buffer at 0x6fa65570:
Offset  Size  Field Name        Type      Description
0x0     4     magic_header      uint      File header magic value
0x4     4     version           uint      Save game format version
0x8     4     flags             uint      Save game flags/options
0xc     4     checksum_crc32    uint      CRC32 checksum of game state
0x10    323   game_state_data   byte[323] Compressed game state buffer
0x14f   -     END               -         Total: 335 bytes (0x14f)

0x6FA4F5A0.name: SetFlagIfNonzero
0x6FA4F5A0.comment:
Conditionally sets bit 0x2 in global flag at 0x6fa65594 if input value is nonzero.

Algorithm:
1. Test if input parameter (in EAX) is zero
2. If zero, skip flag modification and return immediately
3. If nonzero, set bit 0x2 in global flag dword at 0x6fa65594
4. Return to caller

Parameters:
  conditionValue - Input test value in EAX register; nonzero means set flag bit

Returns:
  void - No return value; modifies global state

Special Cases:
  If EAX is zero, global flag is left unchanged
  If EAX is nonzero, bit 0x2 is set (OR operation preserves other bits)

0x6FA4F5B0.name: InitializeGameStateBuffer
0x6FA4F5B0.signature: void InitializeGameStateBuffer(char modeType, void * pGameStateData, ushort controlFlags)
0x6FA4F5B0.comment:
Initialize game state buffer with mode, data, and control flags.

Algorithm:
1. Clear 212-byte buffer at 0x6fa65570 (offset 0x80 * 4 + 4 bytes)
2. Set magic header (0xaa55aa55) and size field (0x60)
3. Copy game state data using CopyMemoryWithAlignment
4. Store mode type and initialize flags with control flags OR 0x1
5. Set initial time value via __time32
6. Check if mode is 0x05 or 0x06 and set flag 0x20 if true
7. Encode mode-specific value (0xd) into encoded buffer
8. Copy 4 dwords of reference data from 0x6fa64d9c to buffer
9. Loop 11 times copying bytes from reference table
10. Set next byte to (modeType + 1)
11. Initialize 8 dwords with 0xffffffff sentinel values
12. Initialize 9 bytes with 0xff sentinel values
13. Set byte at offset 0xd to 0x01
14. Encode control flags and 0x00 into encoded format
15. Set final 3 bytes to 0xff and terminator to 0x00

Parameters:
modeType (char, CL): Game state mode identifier (0x05, 0x06, or other)
pGameStateData (void*): Pointer to source game state data to copy
controlFlags (ushort): Control/status flags to store (bit 0 always set to 1)

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Mode 0x05 and 0x06: Trigger flag bit 0x20 (render enabled)
- Magic value 0xaa55aa55 is buffer signature/header
- Size field 0x60 specifies buffer footprint
- Encoded sections use EncodeValueAsSignedBytes for 2-byte encoding
- Multiple sentinel blocks (0xffffffff and 0xff) indicate unused fields
- Final structure is approximately 212+ bytes

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field Name          | Type    | Description
-------|------|---------------------|---------|-------------------------------------------------------
0x0    | 4    | Magic               | uint    | Signature 0xaa55aa55
0x4    | 4    | Size                | uint    | Buffer size (0x60)
0x8    | 128  | StateData           | uint*4  | Copied game state (via CopyMemoryWithAlignment)
0x18   | 4    | Flags               | uint    | Control flags (input OR 0x1)
0x1c   | 1    | ModeType            | char    | Mode identifier from param
0x20   | 1    | InitFlag            | char    | Always 0x1
0x22   | 4    | TimeValue           | uint    | Result from __time32()
0x26   | 4    | Unknown1            | uint    | 0x14f
0x2a   | 1    | Field3              | char    | 0x10
0x2b   | 1    | Field4              | char    | 0x1e
0x2c   | 16   | ReferenceData       | uint*4  | Copy from 0x6fa64d9c-0x6fa64dac
0x3c   | 11   | DataArray           | char*11 | Copied from reference table
0x47   | 1    | ModeInc             | char    | modeType + 1
0x48   | 32   | Sentinels1          | uint*8  | 0xffffffff markers
0x68   | 9    | Sentinels2          | char*9  | 0xff markers
0x71   | 1    | Marker              | char    | 0x01
0x72   | 2    | Encoded1            | char*2  | Encoded flags value
0x74   | 2    | Encoded2            | char*2  | Encoded 0x00
0x76   | 3    | Sentinels3          | char*3  | 0xff markers
0x79   | 1    | Terminator          | char    | 0x00

0x6FA4F700.name: GetGameInitializationCallbackFlag
0x6FA4F700.comment:
Retrieves the current state of the post-game initialization callback flag.

Algorithm:
1. Load the global callback flag from DAT_6fa65e90 into EAX
2. Return the flag value to caller

Parameters:
  (none)

Returns:
  uint - Callback flag value (0=not set, non-zero=callback pending and should be dispatched)

Special Cases:
  * Global location DAT_6fa65e90 is shared with other initialization functions
  * When non-zero, indicates that post-game session cleanup/callback dispatch is required
  * Used by DispatchGameCommand to determine if final callback handler execution is needed

0x6FA4F710.name: CompletePostGameInitialization
0x6FA4F710.comment:
Post-game initialization completion callback that signals successful rendering queue processing.

Algorithm:
1. Return success status code

Returns:
  int - Status code (1 = success/complete)

Special Cases:
  * Called as a rendering queue callback after post-game initialization sequence
  * Simple stub function that always returns 1
  * Used in DispatchGameCommand to signal completion of post-game setup operations

0x6FA4F720.name: CompareObjectFieldsAndModifyBitfield
0x6FA4F720.comment:
Compares two object fields and modifies a bitfield based on the comparison results.

Algorithm:
1. Load two global object references from fixed memory addresses
2. Validate and retrieve the first Unicode string field using ValidateAndGetObjectField
3. Validate and retrieve the second Unicode string field using ValidateAndGetObjectField
4. Call strlen on the first string through function pointer at 0x6fa5c050
5. Compare string length result: set ESI to 1 if length > 0, else 0
6. Call strlen on the second string through function pointer at 0x6fa5c050
7. Compare string length result: set EDX to 1 if length > 0, else 0
8. Combine results: ESI |= EDX (bitwise OR)
9. Pass combined boolean result to ModifyObjectBitfield and jump to that function
10. Function does not return (tail-call to ModifyObjectBitfield)

Parameters:
None (uses global state at 0x6fa65e84, 0x6fa65e88, 0x6fa65e8c)

Returns:
Indirect via ModifyObjectBitfield (tail-call, no direct return)

Special Cases:
- Global memory addresses 0x6fa65e84, 0x6fa65e88, 0x6fa65e8c hold object references
- Function pointer at 0x6fa5c050 is called with ECX parameter (likely Unicode::strlen)
- Uses SETG instruction to convert sign comparison to boolean (1 if positive, 0 otherwise)
- Result is OR'd together: condition is true if EITHER string length is > 0
- __stdcall convention: stack cleaned by callee

0x6FA4F770.name: SetGameInitializationFlag
0x6FA4F770.comment:
Sets the global game initialization flag and invokes rendering state initialization.

Algorithm:
1. Set game_initialization_flag (0x6fa65e90) to 1 (indicating game is initialized)
2. Call InitializeRenderingState to set up rendering subsystem
3. Return 1 (success status code)

Parameters:
None

Returns:
uint: Always returns 1 (success indicator)

Special Cases:
- Flag at 0x6fa65e90 is checked by GetGameInitializationCallbackFlag
- Used as completion signal for game initialization sequence
- InitializeRenderingState handles actual rendering setup

Context:
This is a gate function that marks game initialization as complete and triggers
rendering state initialization. The global flag at 0x6fa65e90 is referenced by
DispatchGameCommand, GetGameInitializationCallbackFlag, and other initialization
handlers to coordinate startup sequence.

0x6FA4F790.name: InitializeRenderingSystem
0x6FA4F790.comment:
Initializes the rendering system by invoking virtual method and state setup.

Algorithm:
1. Load global rendering context pointer from 0x6fa656c4
2. Load rendering parameters address (0x6fa5e256) into ECX
3. Call virtual method at offset 0xb8 in rendering context object
4. Call InitializeRenderingState function to complete initialization
5. Return 1 to indicate successful initialization

Returns:
1 - Initialization completed successfully

Special Cases:
- RET 0x4 indicates __stdcall convention with hidden parameter on stack
- Global at 0x6fa656c4 must be initialized before this function is called
- Called from FUN_6fa4fe00 during game initialization sequence

0x6FA4F7B0.name: ValidateEmailFormat
0x6FA4F7B0.comment:
Validates email address format by checking for @ and . characters with proper positioning.

This function performs basic email format validation by ensuring the email address contains
both an @ symbol and a dot, with correct spacing requirements. It validates that there is
at least one character before the @, at least one character between @ and ., and at least
one character after the dot.

Algorithm:
1. Check if input string pointer is NULL - return 0 if NULL
2. Search for @ character (0x40) in the string
3. If @ not found, return 0 (invalid)
4. Search for . character (0x2e) starting from @ position
5. If . not found, return 0 (invalid)
6. Verify at least one character before @ (string start < @ position)
7. Verify at least one character between @ and . (@ + 1 < . position)
8. Get full string length using CalculateStringLength
9. Verify . is not at end of string (string length > . position + 1)
10. Return 1 if all validations pass, 0 otherwise

Parameters:
  pEmailString: Pointer to null-terminated email address string to validate

Returns:
  1 (true) if email format is valid; 0 (false) if invalid or NULL input

Special Cases:
  - NULL input pointer returns 0
  - Missing @ or . returns 0
  - @ at string start (no local part) returns 0
  - . immediately after @ (no domain) returns 0
  - . at string end (no TLD) returns 0

0x6FA4F800.name: UpdateUIControlState
0x6FA4F800.comment:
Updates the UI control state by dispatching a command handler and rendering status text.

Algorithm:
1. Check if global flag DAT_6fa65548 is enabled; exit if not set
2. Call dispatch handler at offset 0x80 in DAT_6fa656c4 to get command result
3. Use switch table (cases 0-6) to convert command to status code 0x1433-0x1439, default to -1
4. Call ClearResourceState() to reset UI state
5. If status code is not -1 (valid), dispatch command handler with zero parameters
6. Render text box with Unicode text rendering
7. Retrieve current tick count and calculate elapsed time since DAT_6fa65558
8. Format elapsed time in 250ms intervals (0-19 range) using sprintf
9. Call ClearResourceState() again
10. Render final text output in UI control

Parameters: none

Returns: void (no return value)

Special Cases:
- Magic number 0x10624dd3 is used for time calculation precision
- Time interval 0xfa (250ms) divides time into 20 buckets (0-19)
- Result -1 indicates invalid command, which skips rendering
- Character buffer is 256 bytes on stack for formatted time string

Structure Layout:
Global state used:
  DAT_6fa65548: Control enable flag
  DAT_6fa65550: Current status code result
  DAT_6fa65558: Reference tick count
  DAT_6fa656c4: Handler object pointer (+0x80 offset for dispatch)
  DAT_6fa6554c: UI control object
  DAT_6fa5c364: GetTickCount function pointer
  DAT_6fa5e9e0: Format string pointer
  DAT_6fa5e9e8: String constant

0x6FA4F940.name: InitializeUIControlState
0x6FA4F940.comment:
Initializes UI control state by clearing global tracking variables.

This function zeroes out two global data items that track the state of UI controls,
preparing them for fresh initialization. The function is called at startup to ensure
a clean slate for UI state management.

Algorithm:
1. Zero out EAX register using XOR operation (assembly idiom for fast zeroing)
2. Store zero to DAT_6fa65548 (global state variable 1)
3. Store zero to DAT_6fa6554c (global state variable 2)
4. Return to caller

Returns:
  void - No return value, performs initialization side effects

Special Cases:
  None - This is a straightforward initialization routine with no edge cases.
  Called once at startup to establish baseline UI control state.

0x6FA4F950.name: ProcessInitializationAndRenderingState
0x6FA4F950.comment:
Manages initialization and rendering state transitions.

Algorithm:
1. Update UI control state and verify handle
2. Initialize handle if NULL (first time)
3. Wait for handle with timeout
4. Initialize rendering state based on wait result
5. Execute cleanup callback if needed
6. Return success status (1)

Parameters:
(none)

Returns:
Always returns 1 (success)

Special Cases:
- Handle creation can fail (returns NULL)
- WaitForSingleObject can timeout or return 0
- Initialization flag (0x6fa65ea0) controls rendering state
- Multiple callbacks via function pointers in table at 0x6fa656c4

0x6FA4F9B0.name: ValidateEmailAddress
0x6FA4F9B0.comment:
Validates email address format by checking for required '@' and '.' characters.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve email string from object field via ValidateAndGetObjectField()
2. Convert Unicode string to UTF-8 in 256-byte buffer using toUtf()
3. Check string length is greater than 2 (minimum valid email)
4. Execute three nested validation blocks (first, second, third email fields):
   a. Find '@' character (0x40) in email string via FindCharInString()
   b. Find '.' character (0x2e) after '@' position via FindCharInString()
   c. Verify '@' and '.' are in correct positions:
      - Start of buffer < '@' position
      - '@' position + 1 < '.' position
      - '.' position < total string length
   d. If '@' not found or '.' not found, validation fails
   e. Set isValidEmail flag to true only if all conditions pass
5. Call ModifyObjectBitfield() to update object state with validation result

Returns:
void - Modifies object state directly via ModifyObjectBitfield()

Special Cases:
- Empty or NULL email strings return without processing
- Strings with length <= 2 skip all validation (too short)
- Multiple '@' or '.' characters: only first occurrence matters
- Unicode strings automatically converted to UTF-8 for processing
- All three validation blocks execute identical logic (possibly for redundancy or fallback)

0x6FA4FB30.name: ValidateAndProcessEmailString
0x6FA4FB30.comment:
Validates and processes an email-format string with '@' and '.' delimiters.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve Unicode string from object field via ValidateAndGetObjectField()
2. Calculate string length using Unicode::strlen()
3. If string length > 0:
   a. Convert Unicode string to UTF-8 buffer (256 bytes max) using toUtf()
   b. Search for '@' symbol (0x40) in converted string using FindCharInString()
   c. If '@' found, search for '.' (0x2e) after '@' position
   d. Validate positions: buffer < '@' position and '@'+1 < '.' position
   e. If all validations pass, calculate string length via CalculateStringLength()
4. Modify object bitfield using ModifyObjectBitfield()
5. Return void

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Email format requires '@' followed by '.' with valid spacing
- Both '@' (0x40) and '.' (0x2e) symbols must exist and be properly positioned
- String must be non-empty (length > 0)
- Maximum UTF-8 buffer size is 0x100 (256 bytes)
- Sets EBX=1 if email validation succeeds, EBX=0 on failure

0x6FA4FBE0.name: ValidateAndCompareObjectLengths
0x6FA4FBE0.comment:
Validates and compares the lengths of two object fields.

This function retrieves two Unicode string fields from global object pointers,
measures their lengths using strlen, and modifies a bitfield based on whether
both strings are non-empty.

Algorithm:
1. Load first object field pointer from global address 0x6fa65e84
2. Load second object field pointer from global address 0x6fa65e88
3. Call strlen on first field and set flag if length > 0
4. Call strlen on second field and set flag if length > 0
5. Combine both flags using bitwise OR
6. Call ModifyObjectBitfield with combined flag result
7. Return success (1)

Returns:
uint - Always returns 1 (success)

Special Cases:
- Both flags are combined with OR, so modification happens if either string is non-empty
- Function uses __stdcall calling convention with 4-byte parameter cleanup

0x6FA4FC40.name: InitializeGameUIControls
0x6FA4FC40.comment:
Initializes game UI controls for the current game session

Algorithm:
1. Get current tick count and store in DAT_6fa65558
2. Destroy all previously active UI controls by iterating through array at DAT_6fa653c0
   - Iterate while iVar2 < DAT_6fa65e34 (control count)
   - Call DestroyUIControl for each control pointer
3. Reset UI control tracking: DAT_6fa65e34 = 0, DAT_6fa65e40 = 1
4. Create first UI control: ProcessGameCommand(&DAT_6fa63980) → store in controls[0]
   - Set event target and entity bit flags (flag=1) on created control
5. Check if UI count < 0x40 (64 controls max), create second control
   - ProcessGameCommand(&DAT_6fa639b0) → store in controls[1]
   - Set event target and entity bit flags on second control
6. Check if UI count < 0x40, create third control
   - ProcessGameCommand(&DAT_6fa639e0) → store in controls[2]
   - Set event target and entity bit flags on third control
7. Initialize rendering state
   - dispatch_command_handler(0,0,0) - Clear command queue
   - RenderTextBoxUnicodeText(0,0,0) - Initialize text rendering
8. Check if UI count < 0x40, create fourth control
   - ProcessGameCommand(&DAT_6fa63a10) → DAT_6fa65548
9. Check if UI count < 0x40, create fifth control
   - ProcessGameCommand(&DAT_6fa63a40) → DAT_6fa6554c
10. Initialize state for game session
    - DAT_6fa65550 = 0xffffffff (sentinel value)
    - DAT_6fa65554 = 0 (clear flag)
    - DAT_6fa6552c = SetGameInitializationFlag
    - UpdateUIControlState() - Finalize UI state
11. If any check fails at capacity limit (0x40): abort with error message

Returns:
- void (no return value; aborts process on error)

Special Cases:
- UI capacity limit: 0x40 (64) controls maximum enforced at each stage
- Control array: DAT_6fa653c0 stores pointers to created UI controls
- Control count: DAT_6fa65e34 tracks number of active controls
- Failure handling: GetReturnAddress(0x60d) + CleanupAndAbort + _exit(-1)
- Control array access: (&DAT_6fa653c0)[DAT_6fa65e34] = uVar1 pattern adds to array
- Rendering initialization must occur after first 3 controls created
- Session flags: 0xffffffff in DAT_6fa65550 marks game session start

Structure Layout:
UI Control Array (at DAT_6fa653c0)
Offset  Size  Field           Type      Description
0x0     0x4   controls[0]     void*     First UI control pointer
0x4     0x4   controls[1]     void*     Second UI control pointer
0x8     0x4   controls[2]     void*     Third UI control pointer
0xC     0x4   controls[3]     void*     Fourth UI control pointer
0x10    0x4   controls[4]     void*     Fifth UI control pointer
...
0x100           Total size (64 pointers)

0x6FA4FDF0.name: ValidateEmailAndReturnSuccess
0x6FA4FDF0.comment:
Validates email string and returns success status.

Algorithm:
1. Call ValidateAndProcessEmailString() to validate email address
2. Return 1 (success indicator)

Parameters:
None

Returns:
1 - Always returns success status (0x1)

Special Cases:
This is a simple wrapper function that delegates to ValidateAndProcessEmailString() and always returns success. Used in InitializeBattleNetCommands as part of the command queue initialization sequence.

0x6FA4FE00.name: HandleGameStateExit
0x6FA4FE00.comment:
Handles exiting current game state and transitioning to main menu or previous state.

Algorithm:
1. Dispatch initial command handler with state identifier 0x2b5e
2. Destroy all active UI controls to clear current interface
3. Enqueue and process game command 0x119, modify entity bit flags
4. Configure first state transition (0x2b61) with function pointer 0x6fa4f790
5. Enqueue and process game command 0x11b, modify entity bit flags
6. Configure second state transition (0x13ef) with function pointer 0x6fa54de0
7. Enqueue and process game commands 0x11c and 0x11f, modify flags for each
8. Render Unicode text message to display state change
9. Return success status (1)

Parameters:
pGameState (EDI) - Game state context or identifier, passed implicitly

Returns:
int - Status code, 1 for success

Special Cases:
Magic numbers represent command codes: 0x2b5e (dispatch), 0x119, 0x11b, 0x11c, 0x11f (state transitions)
Global addresses store state configuration: 0x6fa64448, 0x6fa64444, 0x6fa64450 (first transition)
                                          0x6fa64478, 0x6fa64474, 0x6fa64480 (second transition)

0x6FA500C0.name: ProcessGameInitializationSequence
0x6FA500C0.comment:
Processes the game initialization command sequence, executing 10 sequential commands.

Algorithm:
1. Clear initialization flag and initialize command queue structure
2. Check if queue position exceeds limit (0x40=64); abort if exceeded
3. Execute command 1 from global array (0x6fa64580), store result at queue[pos]
4. Dispatch command handler (const 0x2b55) and render text box UI
5. Check queue limit before command 2; proceed if within bounds
6. Execute command 2-4 sequence with queue position increments and UI updates
7. Execute command 5 with field setter flag (0x6fa4fbe0) applied to result
8. Execute command 6-7 sequence with nested queue checks and field operations
9. Execute command 8 with field setter applied (result stored at 0x6fa65e88)
10. Execute command 9 (0x6fa646a0) and final validation sequence
11. On queue overflow at any stage: abort with error message and exit code -1
12. Otherwise: set active UI control, link structures bidirectionally
13. Retrieve and validate two text fields from entity objects
14. Apply string length checks and bitfield modifications to entity

Parameters:
  None - All command data accessed through global command array pointers

Returns:
  void - Function never returns to caller; delegates to final handler or exits via _exit()

Special Cases:
  Commands 5, 7, 8 trigger special field setter operation (0x6fa4fbe0)
  Magic constants 0x2b55-0x2b58 passed to command handlers
  Queue overflow boundary at 0x40 (64) checked after each command
  Final validation path involves bidirectional structure linking
